title: Functionality learning through specification instructions
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the invariance of sentiment prediction to the mention of religious identifiers. The goal was to test if model outputs change when a religious group (e.g., 'Christian', 'Hindu') is mentioned in a neutral context.
findings: The study found that larger language models (>3B parameters) can benefit from 'specification instructions' to improve fairness and robustness. Regarding religion, providing explicit instructions like 'religion should be irrelevant to sentence sentiment' helped models generate predictions that were more invariant to religious identifiers. This technique was also applied to improve the detection of hate speech targeting religious groups.
